author: theo_marchetti
subject: Four-way stop at Harlo and Dunsany? Also, where is the car wash?
body: I moved here last week and I nearly got clipped twice at Harlo Street and Dunsany Road this week. I can't tell who has right of way, and it feels like that corner needs a four-way stop. Also, where is the nearest car wash that isn't a gas station?

comments.author: tomasz_wojcik
comments.body: Dunsany has the stop signs, Harlo doesn't. Harlo traffic goes through and Dunsany traffic yields.

comments.author: dale_hartwell
comments.body: Tomasz is right, though half of Harlo treats the sign like a suggestion. The Village only adds a four-way stop after a traffic count, so ask for one in writing.

comments.author: lupe_ochoa
comments.body: Welcome, Theo! There is a self-serve car wash on Quenby Road with a blue sign, and the bays take quarters and cards.

comments.author: casey_ostrander
comments.body: We walked that corner on Sunday with the stroller, too. Please push for the four-way stop, or at least a flashing light.

author: casimir_lowe
subject: Ashgrove Road, 52 in a 30 by the park while kids were crossing
body: A silver pickup went by at about 52 on Ashgrove Road at the park entrance on Tuesday around 4:40, with three kids crossing alongside the crossing guard. This is the third time this month I have seen it. Someone needs to put a speed trailer out there or we need speed humps, because drivers are not going to slow down on their own.

comments.author: maribel_serrano
comments.body: Casimir, I have counted cars at pickup and it is bad. Ask the Village for a speed trailer, since they lend them out for two weeks at no charge.

comments.author: ansel_grieco
comments.body: Everyone speeds on every road in this town. Casimir, you go 40 on Tennant Pike yourself, so get off your porch and stop blaming the kids.

comments.author: casimir_lowe
comments.body: Ansel, I drive Tennant Pike at the limit, and I have the speedometer receipts to prove it. You defend the drivers because you are one of them.

comments.author: ansel_grieco
comments.body: Speedometer receipts. Listen to yourself, Casimir, you sound like a man with a clipboard and no life.

comments.author: gunnar_sorensen
comments.body: The road is 24 feet wide with no shoulder and a long straight stretch, so it looks like a highway to anyone behind the wheel. You can post 30 all you want, but fix the road design before you blame the drivers.

comments.author: ruth_ellery
comments.body: Two kids and a crossing guard at the park? Dear me. My grandson crosses there every morning. Could we start with a sign board that shows each driver their own speed?

comments.author: leona_brooks
comments.body: Gunnar, the road design is only half of it. People drive like the limit is a suggestion, and I will keep saying so until somebody with a badge does something.

comments.author: gunnar_sorensen
comments.body: Leona, nobody said the rules are optional. I said fix the road, and a badge cannot stop a truck doing 50 on a straight road.

author: benito_ruiz
subject: Brindle Road closed for culvert work starting Monday, October 19
body: Starting Monday, October 19, the Village public works crew closes Brindle Road between Corvan Road and the creek for culvert replacement, about three weeks. The detour runs north on Corvan to Tennant Pike and back east. The bus stop at Brindle and Sayer moves to the corner of Corvan and Pellard Lane, and signs go up Friday.

comments.author: hanna_lindgren
comments.body: The Village notice says the closure starts Monday, October 19, but the sign on Corvan says the 20th. Please check the public works page, because I would like the date fixed before anyone shows up.

comments.author: odessa_wright
comments.body: Thanks for the detail, Benito. Does the Halsey Crossing bus route also use Corvan? I want to know before the kids get on.

comments.author: kofi_mensah
comments.body: Heads up, the Corvan turn at the top of the detour is tight for a box truck. If you are hauling, use Tennant Pike and save three minutes.

comments.author: benito_ruiz
comments.body: Odessa, I asked the transportation office, and the route bus does use the Corvan detour, with the stop at Corvan and Pellard Lane.

author: june_akers
subject: Crosswalk at the Orrin Street school entrance on Millrace Drive needs a flashing beacon
body: The crosswalk by the Orrin Street school entrance on Millrace Drive has faded paint, no flashing sign, and the buses turn in at the same spot. Yesterday a car did not stop for the crossing guard with two kids in the lane. I would like the Village to add a flashing beacon before winter. Who do we email?

comments.author: maribel_serrano
comments.body: Email public works and cc the school principal, and include the date, the time, and the make of the car if you have it. Then ask for a traffic count, since the Village needs one before it funds a beacon.

comments.author: owen_pruitt
comments.body: Every bus driver on Millrace turns in at the same time I am trying to leave for work. A flashing beacon would at least give the cars a reason to look up. Good luck with the Village.

comments.author: henrik_dahl
comments.body: A beacon requires a traffic study, and the study costs money. Check the signals line in the capital plan before you expect anything this year.

comments.author: mateo_gallegos
comments.body: I can walk the kids to the corner on Thursdays if a few parents want to start a crossing group. Message me and we will sort out times.

comments.author: owen_pruitt
comments.body: Henrik, the capital plan has no signals line at all, page 42 is sidewalk repairs. You are reading the wrong book.

author: hal_brenneman
subject: Snow plow routes posted for the winter, my cul-de-sac is not on the list
body: The Village posted the snow plow route map this week. I went through it twice with my reading glasses, and the Vennor Court cul-de-sac is not on it, and neither is the loop behind the old depot. My truck won't turn around in a plowed-in drive, so do I have to shovel the end of my driveway twice? Is there a process for adding a street?

comments.author: tomasz_wojcik
comments.body: Call public works and ask for the plow route change request form. They add a cul-de-sac when there are at least four houses on it, and Vennor has nine.

comments.author: hal_brenneman
comments.body: Tomasz, nine houses is a parade, and I will get that form before the first frost. It is on the website, buried under Forms, then Public Works, then Other.

comments.author: yusuf_karimi
comments.body: The plow priority list is in the same packet: arterials first, then bus routes, then cul-de-sacs. Expect up to 24 hours of lag after a storm.

comments.author: dale_hartwell
comments.body: Don't park on the street during a plow. That's how the blade ends up in your bumper, ask me how I know.

author: marisol_quintero
subject: Power out on Tennant Pike and both sides of Sayer Lane since 5 am
body: The power went out around 5:10 this morning on the north side of Tennant Pike and on both sides of Sayer Lane. I called the outage line, and it says crews are assigned with restoration estimated for 1 pm. The kids are in pajamas with no heat, so if you have a generator, please keep it outside and you might be the hero today.

comments.author: samir_qureshi
comments.body: Ours is out in Ember Fields too. Is the 1 pm estimate from the utility, or from the town?

comments.author: marisol_quintero
comments.body: From the utility line, which says 1 pm, but the woman on the phone said early afternoon. Plan for 1 and be pleasantly surprised if it comes sooner.

comments.author: curtis_bell
comments.body: When the power comes back, switch appliances on one at a time, and keep the fridge shut until it has been back a while. If anyone depends on medical equipment, call the utility now and ask for priority status.

comments.author: dorothy_breen
comments.body: Sorry, I'm new here and I'm sorry to ask, but who do I call if it is still out after 1? I would rather not bother anyone.

comments.author: gunnar_sorensen
comments.body: If your breaker tripped and the rest of the street is on, call Bramwell Electric before you start poking at the panel. Their tech did ours in an hour on a Saturday, and I will admit it was worth the bill.

author: henrik_dahl
subject: Water rates go up January 1: about $12 a month for a typical household
body: The water department rate ordinance passed 4 to 2 last week. The base charge goes from $19 to $24 a month, and usage goes from $5.80 to $6.90 per 1,000 gallons, effective January 1. For a typical household using 6,000 gallons, that is about $12 a month more, or roughly $140 a year. The new water tower on Corvan is part of the reason.

comments.author: wendell_pike
comments.body: The ordinance is 26-11 and the rate table is on page 2. Henrik has the math right for a 6,000 gallon household, so check it against your own bill.

comments.author: henrik_dahl
comments.body: Wendell, I know the ordinance number, I read it before you did. The tower is still the problem, because the water department cannot say what it costs.

comments.author: shirin_bahrami
comments.body: The tower estimate is in the capital plan at $4.1 million on page 37, with a range attached. That is not the same as cannot say.

comments.author: ivan_kuzmenko
comments.body: If you have a running toilet, fix that first. A new flapper is about $8 and can save thousands of gallons a year, so check your meter before the rate change hits.

comments.author: priya_lakhani
comments.body: Thank you for the plain-dollar math, Henrik. It is the first thing I have read on this that I could actually check against my own bill.

author: lena_hoffer
subject: Internet down since 11 pm, modem light blinking orange
body: Is anyone else's internet out since last night? Mine has been down since about 11 pm, and the modem light is blinking orange. Support says there may be a line problem in the area, but I'm not sure. I am new here, so sorry if this is a dumb question.

comments.author: noel_brandvold
comments.body: Welcome, Lena! An orange light usually means no signal reaches the modem from the line, not that the modem is broken. Ask them for a signal test and write down the ticket number.

comments.author: kofi_mensah
comments.body: Mine has been fine on my end, so it's probably the line on your side. Hope it's back up soon, Lena!

comments.author: walt_gerrity
comments.body: Back in the nineties the whole Greaves line went out for three days, and they fixed it with a man on a ladder and a thermos of coffee. Things are faster now, but the process is much the same.

comments.author: lena_hoffer
comments.body: Thanks, Noel, I'll call them this morning and write down the ticket number. Thank you all for the help.

comments.author: renata_ocampo
comments.body: Summary so far: check the modem light, call the provider line, ask for a signal test, and keep the ticket number. Lena, if it's still out next week, post the ticket here and we will help chase it.

author: eli_stroud
subject: Trash skipped on Corran Avenue AGAIN!!! third Tuesday in a row
body: Trash got skipped on Corran Avenue again!!! Third Tuesday in a row. The bins were still out at 6 pm and the hauler says the route is 'delayed,' whatever that means. Who do I even email?? The recycling cart has been in my driveway since the Fourth of July.

comments.author: mateo_gallegos
comments.body: Email the public works desk with the address and dates, then cc the Village manager. Send photos of the bins with the timestamps on them.

comments.author: owen_pruitt
comments.body: The bus driver got our route on Thursday and somehow not on Tuesday. The hauler is clearly running on the school bus schedule.

comments.author: june_akers
comments.body: My neighbor's bin was skipped too, and she was told the truck broke down. Keep a log with dates, because it helps when they say the route is delayed.

comments.author: henrik_dahl
comments.body: The hauler contract was renewed in March at a higher rate, see page 9 of the agreement. Ask the Village why they pay more for fewer pickups.

comments.author: cyrus_mehta
comments.body: I was up late and saw the garbage truck drive past our block at 12:40 am on that Tuesday, with the lights off. Maybe they are running a night route nobody told us about, and I can send you my log if it helps.

author: gabriel_nunez
subject: Water main break at Tennant Pike and Ilsted Way, no water across Halsey Crossing
body: Big water main break at Tennant Pike and Ilsted Way. Water has been out across most of Halsey Crossing since about 6 am, and crews are on site. There is a boil advisory for everyone south of the creek until tests come back, so do not drink or cook with tap water. Bottled water is running low at the shops, and I am keeping the oven off until we have water back.

comments.author: curtis_bell
comments.body: Crews are on it, and the boil advisory is the right call. Boil the water for a full minute at a rolling boil, or use bottled water for drinking and brushing teeth.

comments.author: odessa_wright
comments.body: Pruett Hardware on Cassidy Mill Road still had cases of bottled water when I stopped by at 9 am, so I bought two. Thanks for the heads up, Gabriel.

comments.author: remy_castellano
comments.body: Is it safe for the baby's bottles? I am so worried, and I don't know if I need to boil the formula water too.

comments.author: jonah_fitch
comments.body: Love that the water main chose a Thursday morning. Does the Village put a timeline on these, or do we just wait and see?

comments.author: bernadette_hughes
comments.body: Crews usually give a timeline within a few hours, Jonah. The Village website posts updates about every hour during an event like this one.

comments.author: gabriel_nunez
comments.body: Odessa, thank you for buying the water. The oven stays off until the boil order lifts, and then the first round of garlic knots is on the house for the block.

author: ansel_grieco
subject: Congress misses another deadline. Pick a side.
body: Congress can't pass a budget on time, and the people who keep voting for the same team deserve every bit of the mess. Pick a side, or stop pretending you are the reasonable one in the room.

comments.author: tomasz_wojcik
comments.body: Ansel, the people who run Congress are the problem, not the voters on the other team. Maybe read a newspaper before you start a fight on here.

comments.author: otis_whitfield
comments.body: ansel you are a fool if you think one side owns being useless. shut the post or stop typing.

comments.author: bridget_mccourt
comments.body: Tomasz is exactly right and everybody here knows it. Ansel is a grown man who thinks this feed is a debate club, somebody tell him!!

comments.author: ansel_grieco
comments.body: Bridget, nobody asked for your opinion. Go yell at a parking meter, you would be more useful there.

comments.author: lloyd_sutter
comments.body: I have been voting since before you were born, Ansel, and you are still a blowhard. Nothing you post is going to change a single ballot in this county.

comments.author: casimir_lowe
comments.body: Lloyd has a point about the blowhard. Whatever side you are on, Ansel, you go on the attack the minute someone disagrees.

comments.author: gil_fenner
comments.body: Could this feed go one week without a national fight? Half of us came here for the trash schedule, Ansel, and you are the reason I mute everything.

comments.author: ansel_grieco
comments.body: Gil, mute me all you want, the same way you mute anybody who wants accountability.

comments.author: owen_pruitt
comments.body: Everybody on here is wasting their time on this. Ansel, Lloyd, Tomasz, all of you, take it to the group chat.

comments.author: brendan_doyle
comments.body: Owen is right about the group chat. Ansel, you are the loudest guy in town, and nobody has ever called you a good neighbor.

author: augustin_perrault
subject: Congress misses its deadlines every year, and we keep blaming the other side
body: Congress keeps missing its funding deadlines, and every time it happens this feed fills up with the same blame. I would like to hear one specific vote from each side that you are proud of, not a slogan. Show me one member who votes the same way every time and I will show you someone who is not paying attention.

comments.author: casimir_lowe
comments.body: Augustin, I can name a dozen votes that go against the grain, but you will not read them anyway. Give me your sources first.

comments.author: shirin_bahrami
comments.body: Casimir, the voting records are public, and I can link the specific roll calls if anyone names a vote. Asking for specifics is a fair request.

comments.author: leona_brooks
comments.body: Both of you are missing the point. The budget always gets missed because nobody wants to be the one who votes for cuts. Augustin, that is the part you are skipping.

comments.author: augustin_perrault
comments.body: Casimir, name three, and I will read every one of them. Leona, I doubt you have read a single budget resolution all the way through.

comments.author: casimir_lowe
comments.body: Augustin, I read the budget every year. I do not need a lecture from someone who doesn't know what a continuing resolution is.

comments.author: augustin_perrault
comments.body: Then we agree on the lecture part. Casimir, go read the budget, and I will go read the resolution, and we can compare notes in January.
